key_insight: Parallel pairwise entangling gates across neighboring trapped-ion wells could provide an efficient transversal controlled-Z operation for fault-tolerant quantum computing.
engineering_relevance: For selected register sizes, geometric cancellation enables parallel gates faster than sequential two-qubit gates while requiring a significantly smaller two-photon Rabi frequency.
method: Implement simultaneous pairwise entangling operations in a double-well trapped-ion architecture.
Suppress unwanted couplings using tailored dynamical decoupling, with pulse count scaling quadratically with ion number.
Use geometric cancellation to reduce pulse count and evaluate crosstalk in logical Bell-state preparation.
evidence_signal: The study analyzes decoherence and laser-misalignment crosstalk, including their impact on fault-tolerant logical Bell-state preparation between two [[4,1,2]] code blocks.
watch_item: Performance gains depend on register size, while laser alignment, decoherence, and quadratic pulse-count scaling remain implementation concerns.
paper_title: Parallel transversal entangling gates for fault-tolerant trapped-ion quantum computing
